image_description: The image displays the interior of a multi-tiered prison cell block. It features rows of cells stacked vertically (at least two levels visible) with metal barred doors and green-painted frames. A concrete walkway runs along the upper level, supported by a railing system. The walls are made of light-colored concrete or plaster, showing signs of wear. The perspective looks down the length of the corridor, emphasizing the repetitive, institutional architecture.

The perspective lines of the ceiling and floor converge slightly unevenly. The details in the distance become mushy and indistinct rather than maintaining sharp geometric edges, indicating a slight failure in long-range depth consistency.
The texture on the concrete walls is somewhat uniform and lacks the specific micro-details of weathering or paint chipping expected in a real prison, appearing slightly 'smooth' or digitally painted.
